A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UniDFlow study. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including material relocated during v2's reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original UniDFlow benchmark scores, component ablations, efficiency measurements, and qualitative generation and editing results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds reflection-complexity and time-step-conditioning experiments.

M1.justification: Section 3.2.4 corrects the stated editing-loss target from preferred clean text tokens to preferred clean visual tokens. This is a limited correction to the written objective; the backbone, adapters, routing, training stages, and inference procedure remain unchanged, and an implementation change is not established.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on 200 PIE-Bench images covering add/remove, reasoning-based, scene-text, and multi-object edits. This extends the evaluated data within existing editing tasks. The earlier training datasets and benchmark coverage are retained.

E2.justification: v2 Table 5 adds in-context token conditioning and AdLN as evaluated alternatives to the proposed time-step conditioning. Existing benchmark comparators and the DPO/uni-GRPO comparisons are retained; spelling changes such as BAGEL/Begal do not represent new methods.

E3.justification: The new PIE-Bench analysis compares reflection-enabled and reflection-disabled settings across four editing categories using PSNR, SSIM, structural distance, and CLIP similarity for edited and preserved regions. Existing training settings are unchanged. Section 4.1 corrects Qwen2.5-VL from 7B to 3B, matching Table 1 in both versions rather than establishing a changed experiment.

E4.justification: v2 adds targeted tests of whether reflection helps across editing complexities and whether token conditioning or AdLN can replace the proposed normalization (Tables 4–5). Earlier model-size, tokenizer, adapter, loss, training-token, and LoRA-rank analyses remain. The expanded discussion of Figure 14 interprets retained examples rather than adding a new visual ablation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. v2's new description of results as averaged across benchmarks does not introduce repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: UniDFlow's GenEval position and color-attribute scores change from 0.97/0.93 in v1 Table 8 to 0.87/0.83 in v2 Table 9, losing leadership in those columns. The headline ablation DPG-Bench score changes from 91.91 to 91.19, although the Qwen3-4B row remains 91.91. New reflection and conditioning results are added; Tables 1–3, OCRBench scores, and the remaining matched benchmark entries are unchanged.

T1.justification: The definition of Ledit immediately before Equation 9 changes its clean target from y_txt,0 to y_vis,0, repairing the text/visual mismatch in the mathematical objective. Other equations are substantively retained, with no new theorem, proof, or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract changes the claimed benchmark count from eight to six, although the introduction still claims eight. The central contributions—unified discrete flow matching, separate adapters, and reference-based multimodal preference alignment—remain the same. The expanded mRef-DPO contribution statement largely restates its existing formulation.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations linking reflection to localization and preservation in complex edits, token-conditioning weaknesses to diluted signals, and AdLN weaknesses to disruption of pretrained normalization. Appendix D also attributes specific retained visual failures to individual alignment losses. The existing impact and applicability qualifications are substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly specifies lambda_KL = 1.8, and Section 3.2.3 explicitly states the Stage-II parameter composition. These are disclosures rather than demonstrated setting changes. Hardware, training schedules, data quantities, and the curation prompt are retained. The standalone OpenGPT-4o-Image dataset URL is removed while its paper citation remains.

R1.justification: v2 adds Ju et al.'s PnP Inversion citation for PIE-Bench and removes the standalone ChatGPT reference. The substantive positioning against autoregressive, hybrid, discrete-diffusion, and preference-alignment approaches remains unchanged; most bibliography changes are formatting or metadata updates.

P1.justification: v2 revises selected contribution and analysis paragraphs, standardizes terminology, updates author affiliations, and adds acknowledgments. It moves subject-driven generation into the editing discussion, reorders appendix sections, and retains the OCR discussion without its former standalone heading. Most explanatory prose and the main narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially reformats the document into conference style, changing typography, headers, caption placement, spacing, and appendix column structure. It merges the detailed GenEval and DPG-Bench tables, adds the reflection table, expands the ablation display, and resizes or relocates numerous figures. The qualitative examples and existing plotted analyses are retained.

improvement.justification: The new reflection and conditioning experiments provide useful support for existing design choices, while the corrected editing-loss target and disclosed KL weight improve specification. These are limited gains. Reporting inconsistencies remain: reduced GenEval scores are not reconciled with the retained uniform-improvement interpretation, and v2 Table 5 still gives different DPG-Bench values for its headline UniDFlow and Qwen3-4B rows.
